To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TAX1BP1 deficiency in mice leads to age‐dependent inflammatory valvulitis through selective NF‐kappa B activation.
TAX1BP1 deficiency causes premature death in mice due to age‐dependent inflammatory valvulitis through selective NF‐kappaB activation.

(i) TAX1BP1 inhibits NF‐κB activity by binding to mono‐ or polyubiquitin and TRAF6; (ii) TAX1BP‐1−/− mice are hypersensitive to TNF‐α/IL‐1β‐mediated inflammatory cardiac valvular damage; and (iii) TAX1BP is an important negative regulator of NF‐κB in the heart.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of TAX1BP1 as a negative regulator of inflammatory NF‐κB‐mediated responses and its role in the pathology of inflammatory valvulitis and TNF‐α hypersensitivity.
the role of TAX1BP1 in NF‐κ‐B activation and the development of cardiac valvulopathy in a TAX1BP1 knockout mouse model.
the role of TAX1BP1 in regulating NF‐κB‐mediated inflammation, and the consequences for mice lacking TAX1BP1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Tax1‐Binding Protein 1 (TAXB1P1) acts in NF‐kB signalling as an essential adapter between A20 and it’s targets, and that TAX1BP1 deficient mice develop an age‐dependent inflammatory disease.
TAX1BP1 deficiency leads to cardiac inflammation by activating NF‐κB.
TAX1BP1 functions as a negative regulator of NF‐κB, and that TAX1BP domain is required for TAX1BP‐mediated regulation of TNF‐induced NFκB signalling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TAX1BP1, by acting as a negative regulator of NF‐κB, is required for maintaining cardiac valvular homeostasis.
TAX1BP1 deficiency leads to selective activation of the NF‐κB pathway in the heart, resulting in inflammatory valvulitis.
TAX1BP1, a ubiquitin‐interacting protein, is a critical negative regulator of TNFR1 and IL‐1R‐mediated NF‐κB and inflammatory responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TAX1BP1 plays a critical role in maintaining homeostasis by preventing excessive NF‐κB‐mediated inflammatory responses.
TAX1BP1, which is highly conserved in vertebrates, is a novel negative regulator of NF‐κB, and that its loss causes a severe inflammatory cardiac valvular disease in mice.
TAX1BP1, by acting as a molecular scaffold, coordinates A20 function and thereby regulates NF‐κB‐dependent inflammation.
